content: 1. A head-to-head comparison is represented in Figure 18, which shows a network diagram of trials reporting treatment-emergent serious adverse events. In this diagram, circles (nodes) represent individual treatments, and lines between the circles indicate the availability of direct comparative evidence between two treatments. The numbers on the lines correspond to the number of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) informing each head-to-head comparison. 2. Figure 19 illustrates a network diagram of trials reporting treatment-related adverse events. Similar to Figure 18, circles represent individual treatments, lines between the circles indicate the availability of direct comparative evidence, and the numbers on the lines denote the number of RCTs informing each comparison. 3. Figure 20 presents a network diagram of trials reporting treatment-emergent adverse events. As with the previous figures, circles represent individual treatments, lines between the circles indicate the availability of direct comparative evidence, and the numbers on the lines represent the number of RCTs informing each comparison. 4. For DRV/r + 2 NRTIs, the values represent the effect of the treatment lower on the diagonal compared to the one higher on it. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. Odds ratios above 1 suggest higher efficacy in viral suppression. 5. For LPV/r + RAL induction, the threshold was <50 copies/ml for the EARNEST and SECOND-LINE trials, but 400 copies/ml for the SELECT trial. The values represent the effect of the treatment lower on the diagonal compared to the one higher on it. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. Odds ratios above 1 suggest higher efficacy in viral suppression. 6. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. Odds ratios above 1 suggest higher proportions of mortality. 7. For DRV/r + 2 NRTIs, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients with AIDS-defining illnesses. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 8. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients discontinuing treatment. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 9. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients discontinuing treatment due to adverse events. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 10. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients with treatment-related serious adverse events. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 11. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients with treatment-emergent serious adverse events. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 12. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients with treatment-related adverse events. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 13. For LPV/r, the values represent the effect of the row treatment relative to the column treatment. Odds ratios above 1 indicate higher proportions of patients with treatment-emergent adverse events. Bold values indicate statistically significant comparisons. 14. DRV/r refers to ritonavir-boosted darunavir, DTG refers to dolutegravir, and LPV/r refers to ritonavir-boosted lopinavir.
